title: Post-Go-Live Performance & Cost Ops Playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
summary: Operational playbook for the first 90 days after enterprise customer go-live focused on latency, throughput, and cost optimization. Includes baselining steps, tuning levers, triage matrix, escalation contacts, and QBR-ready metrics.
content:
Overview:

This playbook helps Customer Success (CS), Site Reliability (SRE), and the customer engineering teams stabilize performance and unit economics after an enterprise go-live on Redwood Inference. It is intended for the first 90 days but is reusable for periodic performance reviews.

Goals:
- Ensure production P95 latency and error rate meet contractual targets.
- Reduce per-token compute cost where possible without degrading quality.
- Establish reliable escalation paths and observable dashboards for stakeholder reporting.

When to use this document:
- Post-go-live in the first 90 days (high-priority).
- Before QBRs to prepare performance and cost slides.
- During performance regressions or unexpected cost spikes.

Key metrics & SLOs (example targets):
- P95 latency (in-region, 512 token context): target <= 300 ms; alert >= 450 ms.
- Request error rate: target <= 0.1%; alert >= 0.5% over 5m.
- KV cache hit ratio: target >= 60%; action < 40%.
- Tokens/sec per GPU (steady-state throughput): baseline target 120k tokens/s for dedicated gpus (varies by model).
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): target depends on committed tier; track delta vs baseline.

Baseline measurement (Day 0–7):
1) Collect workload samples: 5–10 representative request traces covering short, medium, and long contexts (example: 32, 512, 2048 tokens).
2) Run synthetic load with production prompt mixes (use small blast tests then ramp):
   - Script: curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","input":"<sample>"}'
3) Capture metrics: P50/P95/P99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, batching distribution, KV cache hit ratio, tail queue length, and cost estimate.
4) Record baseline table (example layout):

| Context | P50 (ms) | P95 (ms) | KV hit % | tokens/s | cost/1k tokens | Notes |
|---------|----------|----------|---------:|---------:|---------------:|-------|
| 32      | 45       | 120      | 78%      | 140k     | $0.38          | fast RPS paths |
| 512     | 120      | 280      | 62%      | 120k     | $0.60          | typical convo |
| 2048    | 320      | 670      | 35%      | 80k      | $1.10          | long-context heavy |

Tuning levers (ordered by recommended risk profile):
- Caching: implement/review prefix and KV cache settings first. Small prompts benefit most; aim to improve KV hit ratio via client-side prefixing or shared conversation keys.
- Batching: increase batch sizes for non-latency-critical routes. Target average tokens per batch > 256 where possible.
- Model variant routing: use a lower-cost quantized variant for background tasks; keep high-fidelity model for critical routes.
- Quantization profiles: enable 4-bit quantization on compatible models after validation on a small eval prompt set.
- Sequence length caps: enforce sensible max_input_tokens and max_completion_tokens per route.
- Rate-limiting & prioritization: route user-facing low-latency requests to low-latency pools; batch background jobs.
- Autoscaling and reservation: adjust Dedicated pool size and burst policy to match steady-state traffic and predictable peaks.

Operational runbook: triage matrix (fast path):
1) Symptom: increased P95 latency (> alert threshold)
   - Check 0–5m: Query Redwood Console dashboard for model-specific P95, queue length, and GPU utilization.
     - If queue length high & GPU utilization < 90% -> likely batching inefficiency (increase batch window or batchable traffic).
     - If GPU utilization > 95% and sustained -> request capacity (auto-scale or open Dedicated change) or enable model variant fallback.
     - If KV hit ratio dropped > 20% -> investigate prompt prefixing change or new user behavior.
   - Remediation steps: temporarily enable cheaper model variant for non-critical traffic, increase autoscaler target, or throttle background jobs.

2) Symptom: sharp cost spike (daily cost > 30% of baseline)
   - Check: per-route token consumption, embeddings vs generation mix, continuous vs batch jobs.
   - Remediation: disable noisy background routes, enable caching for embeddings, review quantization profile.

3) Symptom: elevated error rate (>= 0.5%)
   - Check: 5xx vs 4xx breakdown, auth failures, malformed payloads, model health.
   - Remediation: rollback recent client or server changes, restart serving pool, open bug with engineering if model runtime errors are recurring.

Escalation path (contact chain):
- Tier 1 CS (oncall): assigned CSM (customer success manager) — contact via Slack #cs-oncall and PagerDuty.
- Tier 2 SRE: eng-sre oncall rotation — page via PagerDuty with subject 'Post-Go-Live Performance Incident: <customer>'.
- Tier 3 Runtime Eng: runtime-owner@example.redwood.com — escalate when GPU-level faults, kernel OOMs, or profiling indicates runtime bug.
- Enterprise escalation: VP Customer Success and CTO if SLA breach is imminent.

Provide these fields in the PagerDuty page: incident_type, customer_name, cluster_id, model, observed_p95, baseline_p95, KV_hit, cost_delta, recent_deploy_commit.

Pre-approved mitigation actions (CS can execute):
- Apply route config override to reduce max_context_tokens to a safe cap.
- Switch traffic on a route to 'variant-low-cost' for X% of requests (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Increase autoscaler min_replicas for the dedicated pool by N (N=1–3 depending on pool size).

Canary rollback and rollout checklist:
1) Validate change in staging with production-weighted traces.
2) Start 10% traffic for 15 minutes, monitor P95 and error rate.
3) If metrics stable, move to 50% for 15 minutes.
4) Full rollout if stable; otherwise rollback immediately and notify stakeholders.

Automated scripts & queries (examples):
- Query recent P95 by route (example with Console API):
  curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 'https://console.redwood.example/api/v1/metrics?route_id=<route>&window=5m&metric=p95'
- KV cache diagnostic extractor (pseudo):
  rwd-kv-inspect --cluster cluster-a --route <route> --last 1h --output csv
- Cost delta report (daily cron):
  /bin/bash generate-cost-delta.sh --customer <customer> --since 2026-02-01

QBR & reporting templates (what to include):
- Executive summary: availability, response times vs SLA, cost trend, top actions taken.
- Technical appendix: baseline vs current tables for P50/P95/P99, KV hit ratio, tokens/s, autoscaler events.
- Action items & owners: e.g., enable quantization profile by 2026-03-01 (owner: customer eng), validate prompts for cacheability (owner: CSM).

Checklist for first 90 days (owner assignments):
- Day 0–7: Baseline collection and dashboard creation (owner: CSM + CS eng).
- Day 8–30: Implement low-risk levers (caching, batching config) and measure impact (owner: CS eng).
- Day 31–60: Trial quantization on a small test set and review quality metrics (owner: CS eng + Applied ML).
- Day 61–90: Finalize model routing policy and submit recommendations for Dedicated sizing adjustments (owner: SRE + CS).

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- For any incident causing SLA degradation, complete postmortem within 7 days and include: timeline, root cause, mitigations, customer impact, and follow-up actions.
- Store postmortems at /confluence/customer-success-and-support/postmortems/ and link to related QBR slides.

Appendix A — Example route configuration snippet (YAML-style):

route_id: convo-fast
model: rwd-4b
max_input_tokens: 1024
max_completion_tokens: 256
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_wait_ms: 25
  target_tokens_per_batch: 512
cache:
  prefix_cache: true
  kv_cache_policy: LRU
  ttl_seconds: 3600
variant_fallbacks:
  - variant: rwd-4b-quantized
    weight: 0.1

Appendix B — Quick sanity checklist before a QBR slide: 
- Are P95 and cost delta updated for the reporting window?
- Have all mitigations been applied and documented?
- Is there a clear ask from the customer (capacity, product changes, pricing)?

Appendix C — Ownership table (example):
| Role | Responsibility | Contact |
|------|----------------|---------|
| CSM | Customer liaison and first responder | priya.nambiar@redwood.ai |
| CS Engineer | Baseline, configs, run actions | ethan.brooks@redwood.ai |
| SRE | Autoscaling, infra capacity | maya.chen@redwood.ai |
| Runtime Eng | Kernel and model runtime issues | runtime-owner@redwood.ai |

Notes and references:

- Use the dedicated 'cs-go-live' Slack channel for realtime coordination.
